content:
Stephanie Nguyen: where are we landing on “final” RFP security language living? I keep seeing ppl paste from Drive drafts + it’s getting messy. Confluence vs Google Drive?

Avery Johnson: +1. I’m mid-response w/ Continental Telco and they asked “what version is this answer from” 😬

Priyom Das: same on Summit. I have like 3 links: (1) Drive master draft, (2) old Confluence page, (3) random snippet in HubSpot. Which is canonical?

Markus Klein: from SE side: Drive is where we *draft* / iterate. But I’ve been telling AEs to only cite Confluence pages in outbound responses. Otherwise we end up emailing customers “draft language”.

Hannah Schmitt: EMEA adds another wrinkle: residency wording changes a lot. I need something I can point to that’s “approved” and dated.

Olga Petrov: Canonical for approved language = Confluence. Drive docs are working drafts only.
Olga Petrov: If it’s going to a customer / into an RFP response, it should be pulled from the Confluence RFP library (once published) or the Security FAQ page. We need version + last reviewed.

Stephanie Nguyen: ok but today, the RFP library is mostly in Drive (rfp-response-library-master-draft). Confluence has FAQ + some one-pagers. Are we publishing the library to Confluence this week?

Talia Benson: yep — plan is:
- Drive = drafting + redlines
- Confluence = published + “approved for external use”
- HubSpot snippets = mirror of the approved blocks (managed by Isabelle once we cut v1)

Daniel Carter: +1 to that. Also: do NOT send customers Drive links. Evidence + report process is gated; Drive links don’t enforce access / NDA flow.

Jordan Blake: Sales needs a single answer here. I want reps to know: “If it’s not on the Confluence index page, it’s not a claim we’re making.”

Naomi Feldman: + add: please don’t cite roadmap or “coming soon” from internal threads. Only current capabilities. If something is in yellow in the claims matrix, it needs escalation (GRC/Sec review) before it goes out.

Avery Johnson: what should I put in the RFP response when they ask “source / reference” for a statement? Just paste the text, or cite a URL?

Olga Petrov: For questionnaires, paste the approved language block + cite the source as:
“Redwood Inference – Enterprise Security FAQ (Confluence), version YYYY.MM, last reviewed <date>”
If they need audit period / SOC 2 specifics, direct them to the evidence request playbook (under NDA) rather than trying to summarize the report.

Hannah Schmitt: can we standardize the exact citation string? Some customers are picky.

Talia Benson: Proposed standard citation format (use consistently):
- “Source: Redwood Enterprise Security Enablement Kit → [Artifact Name], v2026.02 (Last reviewed: 2026-02-xx), Confluence.”
- If a customer won’t accept “Confluence” as a cite, we can provide a PDF export of the page *after* it’s published (no Drive exports).

Markus Klein: also: for deployment-specific answers (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) make sure to include the mode in the response. We’ve been getting dinged for “applies to all deployments” when it doesn’t.

Priyom Das: can we get a single index link we can bookmark?

Talia Benson: working on it. The Confluence index page is: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SE/Enterprise+Security+Enablement+Kit (will be updated w/ “RFP Response Library” section once published). I’ll drop the final link + version tracker when live.

Isabelle Laurent: On the HubSpot side: once we have the published Confluence blocks, I’ll create snippets named like:
- SEC-RFP-DataRetention-v2026.02
- SEC-RFP-SSO-RBAC-v2026.02
…and lock editing permissions so reps don’t “tweak” them.

Stephanie Nguyen: thank you. Immediate ask: what do we do *this week* while library is still draft in Drive?

Olga Petrov: This week:
1) Use the published Security FAQ page for anything it covers.
2) If the question isn’t covered, ask in #eng-security or route via the exceptions policy. Don’t improvise language.
3) If you must respond under deadline, mark the response as “Redwood provided preliminary response pending final security review” and loop in GRC for approval.

Daniel Carter: + please open an evidence request ticket if they ask for SOC 2 report / pen test report. Do not promise we will share pen test report; we share SOC 2 report under NDA, pen test is summarized language only (unless explicitly approved case-by-case).

Avery Johnson: got it. (reactions: :thumbsup: x4)

Hannah Schmitt: can we add a note to the index page: “Drive drafts are not customer-facing” — this keeps coming up.

Talia Benson: yep adding a banner + a short “what to do / what not to do” section.

Jordan Blake: Action items:
- Talia: publish index + banner + citation format
- Olga/Daniel: confirm the exact “cite string” + versioning policy
- Isabelle: HubSpot snippets after publish
Everyone else: stop using Drive copy in customer responses.

Naomi Feldman: and please flag me if you see answers out there implying ISO 27001 certified. We’re “aligned” / “controls mapped” language only unless GRC says otherwise.

Stephanie Nguyen: 🙏 closing loop: once Confluence is source of truth, we’ll require the version in RFP responses. If someone needs an exception, escalate via the RFP approvals SOP.
